jobs.prompt:
TASK (roadmap R-027 'Split quality is graded'): a pure, read-only module that grades how well a project's tickets were split. Acceptance: 'A Split quality panel per project shows overhead ratio, first-try pass rate, critical path, wave fill, collisions, review $ per ticket and ticket sizes, each green, amber or red.' This job writes ONLY the module and its test; another job wires it into the board. Do NOT touch tools/swarm.mjs.

Write tools/split-quality.mjs (ESM, SPDX header, short header comment). Export `SPLIT_THRESHOLDS` (one frozen table, easy to retune, documented inline) and `async splitQuality({ root, now = Date.now(), slots = null, windowDays = 14 })` that never throws and returns `{ metrics: [ { key, label, value, display, unit, grade: 'green'|'amber'|'red'|'unknown', basis, note } ], grade: worst known grade or 'unknown', at: ISO }` in this fixed order. Inputs: the ticket ledger (readLedger from tools/tickets.mjs), the ticket log .swarm/project/tickets.log (one JSON per line: {at, event:'transition', id, from, to, by, note} and others; read it line by line, skip bad lines), and run states (readRunStates from tools/board-data.mjs is fine, or read .swarm/runs/*/state.json the same way) limited to runs that started within windowDays. A metric with no data gets grade 'unknown' and a `note` saying what is missing (never a fake green).
Metrics and default thresholds (green / amber / else red):
1. overhead: 'Overhead ratio' = jobs in the window that are not first-attempt build work (job.type in review, fix, merge, test-fix, or job.attempt > 1, or job.id matching /(^|-)(review|fix|retry|merge)(-|$)/) divided by all jobs; display as %; green <= 20%, amber <= 35%.
2. firstTry: 'First-try pass rate' = done tickets (status done) whose tickets.log history has no transition into 'blocked' and no transition from 'running' or 'review' back to 'todo' or 'ready'; divided by done tickets; green >= 80%, amber >= 60%.
3. criticalPath: 'Critical path' = longest dependsOn chain (count of tickets on it) among non-cancelled, non-proposed tickets, as % of those tickets; also show 'N of M'; green <= 15%, amber <= 25% (roadmap R-012 uses 25%). Cycles must not hang: guard with a visited set.
4. waveFill: 'Wave fill' = average over the last 6 runs in the window of (jobs in the run / slots), capped at 100%; slots = the `slots` argument (machine worker limit) or, when null, the max jobs any of those runs had; grade unknown when there are no runs; green >= 75%, amber >= 50%.
5. collisions: 'Collisions' = count in the window of: run states whose integration recorded conflicts (any of state.mergeQueue?.conflicts length, state.integration?.conflicts length, state.conflicts length) plus jobs whose status or error mentions 'conflict' (case-insensitive); green 0, amber <= 2, else red.
6. reviewCost: 'Review $ per ticket' = sum of costUsd of review jobs in the window (job.type === 'review' or id matches /review/) divided by tickets done in the window (done times from tickets.log transitions to 'done'); display '$0.12'; green <= 0.25, amber <= 0.75; unknown when no tickets were done in the window.
7. sizes: 'Ticket sizes' = share of counted tickets with size 'M' (or with more than 6 files in ticket.files) ; display like '3 S · 2 M (40% M)'; green <= 30%, amber <= 50%.
Keep each metric's computation in its own small function. Tests: tests/split-quality.test.mjs (node:test, assert/strict, temp project dirs cleaned up, fixtures written as .swarm/project/tickets.json, tickets.log and .swarm/runs/<id>/state.json in the shapes tools/tickets.mjs reads): each metric's value and each grade boundary (green/amber/red) with small fixtures; a dependsOn cycle does not hang; an empty project returns every metric 'unknown' with a note and overall grade 'unknown'; overall grade is the worst known grade. Run `node --import ./tests/_isolate-config.mjs --test tests/split-quality.test.mjs` and `node tools/check-package.mjs`.

TASK: a read-only 'Benchmark scorecard' for Swarm Watch: weekly before/after trend per metric, reading benchmark result files that another orchestrator (the MacBook seat) will write. This job writes the module, its test and the file-format contract; another job wires it into the board. Do NOT touch tools/swarm.mjs.

1) docs/benchmarks-format.md: the contract, plain short words. Files live in the project at docs/state/benchmarks/<YYYY-MM-DD>-<label>.json (label: 'baseline' for the first measurement, else any short [a-z0-9-] word such as 'after' or 'weekly'). Shape: { "version": 1, "at": ISO time, "label": string, "source": short string (e.g. 'bench/throughput' or a commit sha), "metrics": { "<key>": { "value": number, "unit": string (e.g. 'min', '%', '$', 'count'), "better": "lower" | "higher", "label": optional display name } } }. Keys are [a-zA-Z0-9_.-]{1,60}. One file per measurement; files are never rewritten. Give one complete example. Say the board reads only this folder, ignores files that do not match, and that a metric missing from a week simply has no point that week.
2) tools/benchmark-scorecard.mjs (ESM, SPDX header): export `async readBenchmarks(root)` (reads docs/state/benchmarks/*.json; name must match /^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}-[a-z0-9-]{1,40}\.json$/; skip invalid files and list them in `skipped` with a reason; cap at 500 files and 256 KB per file; never throws) and `scorecard(files, { now = Date.now(), weeks = 12 })` (pure) returning `{ metrics: [ { key, label, unit, better, baseline: {value, at} | null, latest: {value, at} | null, change: number|null (latest - baseline), changePct: number|null, verdict: 'better'|'worse'|'flat'|'unknown', weekly: [ { week: 'YYYY-Www' (ISO week), value } ] } ], weeks: ['YYYY-Www', ...], skipped: [...], files: count }`. Baseline = the earliest file labelled 'baseline' that has the metric, else the earliest file with it. Latest = the newest file with it. weekly = for each of the last `weeks` ISO weeks up to now, the value from the newest file in that week having the metric (omit weeks with none). verdict: unknown when baseline or latest missing or they are the same file; flat when |changePct| < 2 (or both 0); better/worse by the metric's `better` direction. Metrics sorted by key. Also export `isoWeek(date)`.
3) tests/benchmark-scorecard.test.mjs (node:test, assert/strict, temp dirs cleaned up): readBenchmarks skips bad names, bad JSON, wrong version, non-number values (each listed in skipped); scorecard picks the 'baseline' file over an earlier non-baseline only when labelled; better/worse/flat for both directions; weekly buckets use ISO weeks across a year boundary (2026-12-31 vs 2027-01-04); weeks without data are omitted; a metric only in later files has baseline = its earliest file. Run `node --import ./tests/_isolate-config.mjs --test tests/benchmark-scorecard.test.mjs` and `node tools/check-package.mjs`.
